properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 27 at 3:04PM HST until October 29 at 5:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
A trough moving over the state from west to east will bring abundant
tropical moisture through at least Wednesday night. Heavy rain and
isolated thunderstorms are expected to produce flash flooding, and
while the greatest flood threat will be focused over Oahu and Maui
County, all islands are at risk.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...All main Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms with intense rain rates
may develop at any time through Wednesday night as a trough moves
over the state from the west. While the greatest flood threat
will be focused over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are at
risk.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE WEDNESDAY NIGHT

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent and gusty northeast winds are slowing river flow. The St
Johns River at Deland is forecast to crest near Minor Flood Stage
through tonight, before beginning a slow decline through the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.0 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent and gusty northeast winds are slowing river flow. The St
Johns River at Astor will remain in Moderate Flood Stage, though
river levels are forecast to slowly decline through this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 3.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.8 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 27 at 8:22PM EDT until October 29 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level in
low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Areas along Bogue Banks beaches, Bogue Sound, the
Newport and White Oak Rivers, and adjacent tidal creeks, and
areas in North Topsail Beach, the lower New River, and
adjacent tidal creeks.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level
is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some
roads and low lying property including parking lots, parks,
lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience
shallow flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will remain high with a King
Tide Cycle in place through Thursday. The morning high tide
will be the highest of the two daily tides.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 2 PM EDT THURSDAY

properties.areaDesc: Northern Outer Banks
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 27 at 8:22PM EDT until October 28 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous
rip currents.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT
Thursday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT
Wednesday through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some roads and
low lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and
homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow
flooding. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will remain high with a King
Tide Cycle in place through Thursday. The morning high tide will
be the highest of the two daily tides.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

out, Coastal waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL out
20 NM, and Coastal Waters From Ochlockonee River to
Apalachicola Fl out to 20 Nm.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EDT /7 PM CDT/ Thursday.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20
to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to
produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous
conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering
response, broaching, overturned dinghies and kayaks, slips and
falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,
and dragging anchors.
properties.instruction:

vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
